key_insight: Correcting dataset biases in binding-affinity datasets — rather than only tweaking model architectures — substantially improves out-of-distribution generalization of predictive models.
problem_solved: Models for binding affinity often overfit to biased training data (e.g., scaffold, target, or assay biases), producing inflated in-distribution performance but poor real-world generalization; the paper addresses detecting and correcting these biases.
method: Identify and quantify dataset biases and leakage (e.g., shared scaffolds/targets between train and test splits) using statistical and fingerprint-based analyses.
Resolve bias via dataset curation and re-splitting strategies (balanced/resampled or de-duplicated splits), plus sample reweighting or augmentation to counter overrepresented patterns.
Re-evaluate models on unbiased, out-of-distribution test sets to demonstrate improved generalization after bias mitigation.
impact: Practitioners gain a practical pathway to improve robustness and real-world utility of binding-affinity models by prioritizing dataset auditing and split design; this leads to more reliable candidate prioritization in drug discovery pipelines.
visual_elements: Before/after schematic: biased train→test leakage vs. bias-resolved, OOD-aware split
Bar chart: performance (MAE/RMSE or R^2) on biased vs. bias-corrected test sets
Heatmap or network showing dataset composition and overrepresented scaffolds/targets
Flowchart: bias detection → curation/reweighting → OOD evaluation
paper_title: Addendum: Resolving data bias improves generalization in binding affinity prediction
paper_authors: David Graber, Peter Stockinger, Fabian Meyer, Siddhartha Mishra, Claus Horn
